title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software

concepts.name: Design Pattern Definition
concepts.definition: Reusable solutions to common problems in software design representing best practices
quotes: Design patterns are reusable solutions to common problems in software design

concepts.name: Factory Pattern
concepts.definition: Creates objects without specifying exact classes, decoupling client code from concrete classes
examples: DatabaseFactory creates MySQL or PostgreSQL connections

concepts.name: Singleton Pattern
concepts.definition: Ensures a class has only one instance with global point of access
trade_offs: Global state can make testing harder

concepts.name: Builder Pattern
concepts.definition: Constructs complex objects step by step, separating construction from representation

concepts.name: Adapter Pattern
concepts.definition: Makes incompatible interfaces work together by converting interface of one class into another

concepts.name: Decorator Pattern
concepts.definition: Adds behavior to objects dynamically without using inheritance

concepts.name: Facade Pattern
concepts.definition: Provides simplified interface to complex subsystem

concepts.name: Observer Pattern
concepts.definition: Defines one-to-many dependency between objects with automatic notification

concepts.name: Strategy Pattern
concepts.definition: Encapsulates algorithms so they're interchangeable at runtime

concepts.name: Command Pattern
concepts.definition: Encapsulates request as an object allowing parameterization and queuing

concepts.name: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
concepts.definition: A class should have only one reason to change

concepts.name: Open/Closed Principle (OCP)
concepts.definition: Open for extension, closed for modification

concepts.name: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
concepts.definition: Derived classes should be substitutable for base classes

concepts.name: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
concepts.definition: Use specific interfaces, not general ones

concepts.name: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
concepts.definition: Depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations

concepts.name: Pattern Categories Framework
concepts.definition: Three main categories organizing design patterns by purpose

concepts.name: Over-Engineering Anti-Pattern
concepts.definition: Applying patterns to simple problems adds unnecessary complexity

concepts.name: Pattern Trade-offs
concepts.definition: Each pattern has benefits and drawbacks that must be understood

concepts.name: Creational Patterns Group
concepts.definition: Patterns dealing with object creation mechanisms

concepts.name: Pattern as Terminology
concepts.definition: Design patterns provide established vocabulary for team communication
